title: Transfer task: defend and revise
target: Support your prediction with measurements and calculations. Show a specific change and explain why you made it.
criteria: Graph the central prediction and coordinate bounds.
Use calculations to support an answer. Explain when the calculation stops working.
Show a specific change and use measurements or details to explain why you made it.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: An object starts at x = 5 m at t = 0. It is predicted to reach x = 17 m at t = 6 s. Which endpoints belong on a straight-line position–time graph of this prediction?
cpa.guide: Plot time horizontally and position vertically, including the nonzero start.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A final coordinate is bounded from 14 to 20 m with central prediction 17 m. Which graph annotation is appropriate?
options: Mark 17 m and the 14–20 m interval at the final time.
Mark only 14 m and call it the exact answer.
Label the interval as 95% probability without a statistical model.
Replace the position axis with force.
cpa.guide: Show the center and bounds without inventing probabilistic meaning.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A simple constant-velocity calculation puts the end of a path far from the origin. Which conclusion can you support?
options: All gravitational effects have been measured.
A single endpoint proves the entire real trajectory.
The real object can never approach Earth.
The predicted endpoint misses the origin within the stated model and bounds.
cpa.guide: Conclusions must be limited to the modeled conditions and evidence.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A calculation predicts a position of 22 m at a given time. The observed position is between 18 m and 20 m. What does this comparison support?
options: Proof that gravity is the only possible cause.
A mismatch requiring checks of assumptions, inputs, or measurement quality.
Exact agreement.
Proof that every measurement is false.
cpa.guide: The prediction lies outside the interval, but cause is not uniquely identified.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A student corrects 600 m/s to 0.600 km/s in a km-based calculation. Which revision note is useful?
options: I removed the original step and claimed it was always correct.
I changed the answer because it looked wrong, with no record.
I corrected the velocity units and recalculated the affected coordinates.
I kept every affected coordinate without checking.
cpa.guide: Document the specific correction and its consequences.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: After fitting a constant-speed calculation to one observed endpoint, what is a useful next test?
options: Claim the fit proves every future position.
Remove uncertainty from all measurements.
Reuse the fitted point as independent validation.
Predict a later position and compare it with a new timed measurement.
cpa.guide: A new observation tests the revised model independently of the point used to fit it.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
